To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed spirometry reference values for the elderly, taking into account their health status.
Spirometry reference values for women and men aged 65–85 living in Southern Europe were derived from a large sample of subjects.

1) we have derived reference values for spirometer variables in a large population of elderly people living in southern Europe; 2) the reference values for FVC and FEV1 are reliable; 3) we have demonstrated that the effect of general health condition is the most important factor influencing spirometric results; and 4) we have shown that a multidimensional assessment of the health status of an elderly subject is necessary for a better interpretation and prediction of spirometry results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the study of the effect of health on spirometry in elderly subjects.

the spirometric values obtained by the present study are reliable reference values for the Italian population of the age range of interest, and that the health conditions of the elderly people should be carefully assessed before interpreting the results of spirometric tests.

the spirometry reference values for women and men aged 65–85 living in Southern Europe, obtained in this study, should be considered in clinical practice, and the health status should be carefully evaluated in the elderly.
the reference values derived in this study should be used for the interpretation of the spirometric results of elderly patients, taking into account their health conditions and their age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of general health status on lung function in the elderly should be carefully considered in the clinical setting.
a good general health status, a good mental condition, and a good physical condition are all associated with a good lung function.
the spirometric reference values obtained from this study can be used to assess lung function in elderly people, taking into account their health condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health status of the individual should be carefully considered in order to correctly interpret the results of spirometry in elderly people.
spirometric values in the elderly are not just the consequence of ageing and of the presence of respiratory diseases but also depend on the general health status.
the health status of an individual is an important determinant of lung function, even in the elderly.
